subject: POC observability plan & success criteria — FintechX
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Lopez <alopez@fintechx.com>, FintechX Evaluation Team <evaluation@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC observability / next steps

Alexandra / FintechX team — thanks again for the call this afternoon. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for the POC observability work: 

1) POC goals / success criteria (high level)
- Validate end-to-end latency under expected load: p50 < 300ms, p95 < 600ms for user-facing calls.
- Errors & correctness: overall error rate < 0.5%; no reproducible quality regressions vs. baseline prompts.
- Cost/efficiency: token cost within 15% of our forecasted baseline for test workload.
- Operational readiness: dashboards, tracing, and log export configured so your SREs can triage incidents within 15 minutes.

2) Observability scope for the POC (what Redwood will deliver)
- Pre-built dashboards (Datadog/Looker): latency by route, tokens per request, model variant split, KV cache hit rate, model fallback count, cost per 1k tokens.
- Tracing: end-to-end request traces with trace ids propagated from your front-end through Redwood runtime (example span: request_router -> model_inference -> response_serializer).
- Logs: structured request/response logs (redacted PII) exported to your Splunk/Datadog ingest endpoint; 30 day retention by default for the POC.
- Metrics: per-model p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (req/sec), error rate, queue length, GPU utilization, batch size distribution, cache hit/miss.
- Alerts: baseline alert rules we recommend (p95 latency increase >30% sustained 5m, error rate >1% sustained 5m, cache hit rate <40%).

3) Who owns what (owners)
- Redwood: create dashboards, tracing instrumentation, log export config, baseline alert rules — owner: Marissa Cole.
- FintechX: provide test workload (traffic replay OR synthetic load), Splunk/Datadog endpoints, and procurement approvals for Dedicated capacity if needed — owner: Alexandra Lopez.
- SRE contact: Tom Reed (we'll loop him into config).

4) Timeline (proposed)
- Aug 6: finalize success criteria and confirm endpoints + service accounts.
- Aug 9: Redwood delivers initial dashboards + tracing config; shared links and a quick walkthrough.
- Aug 12-18: FintechX runs evaluation scenarios (baseline traffic + edge cases).
- Aug 19: Joint review of results; decide next steps (rollout, Dedicated commit, or tweaks).

5) Asks / immediate next steps
- Alexandra: please confirm acceptance of the success criteria above and send Splunk/Datadog ingest endpoint and a service account or write token.
- FintechX: share a sample of representative prompts or a traffic replay (anonymized) by end of day Aug 6.
- Redwood: I'll attach a short observability plan + success criteria spreadsheet after this thread.

I attached a short POC Observability Plan and success criteria workbook. If the above looks good I'll schedule a 30m walkthrough for Aug 9 (proposed 10:00am PT).

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: 20260805-redwood-observability-plan.pdf, 20260805-poc-success-criteria.xlsx

From: Alexandra Lopez <alopez@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FintechX Evaluation Team <evaluation@fintechx.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@fintechx.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: POC observability / next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. We agree with the success criteria and timeline broadly. A few notes/questions from our side: 

- Latency targets: p95 < 600ms is acceptable for the user journeys we discussed, but can you confirm whether that is measured from request arrival at Redwood to token generation completion, or end-to-end at our edge? We prefer end-to-end measurements.
- Cost baseline: we'll send over a 48-hour traffic replay (anonymized) and a representative set of prompts by EOD Aug 6.
- Log export: we can provide a Datadog HTTP intake key (service account) — Tom will share that. We also need to confirm redaction rules for any sensitive fields in the request payloads.

We'd also like the dashboard to include a simple table of recent inference failures with stack traces (masked) and the trace id that can be clicked to open the full trace.

If you can confirm the latency measurement point and the redaction approach, we'll schedule the replay for Aug 10. 

Thanks,
Alexandra
Head of Product Engineering, FintechX
alopez@fintechx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Lopez <alopez@fintechx.com>, FintechX Evaluation Team <evaluation@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC observability / next steps (details on metrics & redaction)

Alexandra — great questions. Quick answers and a more detailed observability checklist below. We'll plan the walkthrough Aug 9 at 10:00am PT unless you request another time.

1) Latency measurement: we will provide both metrics: 
- "inference_latency_redwood" (arrival at Redwood runtime -> inference completion) and
- an optional end-to-end metric if you add a short SDK header/time propagation on your side (we'll instrument the trace to include your edge span).
We'll surface both in the dashboard so you can compare.

2) Redaction approach: Redwood will redact/omit the following fields before forwarding logs: any field labelled "ssn", "card_number", "email" (unless explicitly allowed), and full prompt content will be truncated to the first 128 characters and hashed for deduplication. We will share the redaction regex and a small sample of transformed logs for your privacy team to sign off.

3) Observability checklist (what we'll deliver in the initial drop on Aug 9)
- Dashboards:
  - Overview: total requests, tokens consumed, avg cost per 1k tokens, active model variant breakdown.
  - Latency: p50/p95/p99 per-route, per-model.
  - Errors: 5xx/4xx split, recent failure table with trace_ids.
  - Efficiency: KV cache hit rate, avg batch size, GPU utilization.
- Tracing: propagated trace_id, spans for router/inference/serialize; links to full span logs.
- Logs: structured JSON events; examples of redacted entries; export configured to Datadog (HTTP intake).
- Alerts: pre-configured examples + suggested thresholds (editable).

4) Alerts & playbooks: we'll include a short playbook for triage: what to check first (trace id, model variant, cache hits), and an escalation path (Redwood on-call + your SRE).

5) Timeline & owners (updated)
- Aug 6: confirm redaction rules + provide Datadog intake key (FintechX).
- Aug 9: Redwood drops dashboards and tracing config; 30m walkthrough.
- Aug 10-17: evaluation and runbook validation.
- Aug 19: results review.

Action items: Jordan, Marcus — can you prepare the dashboard links and the sample redacted logs so we can send to Alexandra's privacy team today? Alexandra/Tom — please share the Datadog key and confirm whether we can include "email" in redaction (we default to redacting).

Thanks — attaching the same observability plan and the success criteria workbook again for reference.

Best,
Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
